assign.now: items 1-3 landed: Save saves, Build speaks the seven words, one meaning per name

log.msg: FIX 1 PROVEN. make/page.js named() called an undefined words(); it calls mode_for() now. Drove the JSON box headless: changed notes surface card -> tint, pressed Save, fetched public/imagine/paging/made/notes/page.json off disk and it read surface: tint with all seven words; set it back to card, saved again, the file reads card. Eleven steps, ZERO console errors. The repo is byte-identical to where it started.

FIX 2. Build has no vocabulary of its own any more. config_of()/mode_for() moved into blocks.js beside the words themselves (Make re-exports it); build/words.js DEFAULT_MODE is now the seven words plus blocks; the three controls write navigation/surface/arrangement; step 4 is ARRANGEMENT with the bar's seven values, and the numbered layout the blocks use is DERIVED from it (layout_of) instead of stored as a second key called arrange. Measured on /build/: the JSON box reads the seven words and the control titles read 1 Name, 2 Navigation, 3 Surface, 4 Arrangement, 5 Blocks, 6 Pages, 7 Code.

FIX 2, the honesty half: a control that writes a word has to SHOW it. BuildStage draws the arrangement chrome now - a toolbar, a footer, a side panel, an aside - wearing paging.css own classes, so Build and a real page draw the same picture. And in stage.js an arrangement PANEL stopped being the navigation RAIL: rail-left/rail-right drew the page's children, which is exactly what the vocabulary says a panel is NOT.

FIX 3, one meaning per name. build/words.js BLOCKS -> PIECES (the realm's own BLOCKS is the six building blocks). build/words.js nav_of deleted - blocks.js nav_of is the one. code_for -> code_for_node (a node has blocks and children) and code_for_config (a configuration is seven words). The file-format examples in make/made.js and make/page.js print the seven words instead of style/content/mech.

assign.now: items 4-8 landed; sweeping the realm at four widths next

log.msg: FIX 4, everything sendable. The nine cross cells are links to /imagine/paging/?navigation=X&arrangement=Y&content=article - safe to wrap because paging.css already puts pointer-events: none on a miniature inside a shot frame. And they DID NOTHING when clicked in-app, for two reasons the url seam did not know about: core's Router pushes the address after the page draws (so url.js now records the CLICKED link in the capture phase), and a page here is BUILT ONCE (so Paging.activated() re-reads the address on arrival, and the realm's front page - which never activates, because core only activates what changed - watches for a click on its own url instead). Measured: a cell click now lands on paging-nav-rail paging-arr-bar-top; the rail's home link resets it.

FIX 4, the nest. presets.js nest is a PRESET ID now, not a longhand config, because ?nest= can only name one of the twelve. Measured on /library/nest/: one lit chip reading 'A dashboard with a left rail', an 'open it on its own' link to /library/dashboard/, and clicking the chip takes the nested page out. The page's own nest survives navigating away and back (base_nest).

FIX 5. Code and More are two different drawers now: Code puts the code box FIRST (200px down an 842px rail), More leaves it last (1551px down). I tried scrolling first and it RACES - code.js highlights asynchronously, the block above grows after the scroll, and the code landed 765px down an 800px rail. Order is not a race. The Library's 'PICK ONE OF TWELVE' chip-button is gone: the bar has an eighth labelled dropdown, PAGE SHAPE, reading the running preset's name; picking one navigates through core's Router. And the drawer's arrangement sentences say 'Inside the box the blocks are one column' before naming layout 1.stack.

FIX 6, wide screens, measured. /stage/ /skin/ /arrangement/ /mechanisms/swap/ opened on an article, whose prose is capped at the 720px reading measure inside a 2739px box - 26 percent. They open on content that uses the width now (a card wall; the dashboard on /skin/, whose small tiles leave the content colour visible around them). 2634px of 2739 = 96 percent. The comparison is live: /content/article/, which IS the article page, still reads 720 of 2739. One more rule was needed - .paging-wall used auto-fill, which KEEPS its empty tracks, so six cards sat in the first six of eleven columns; auto-fit collapses them.

FIX 7 and 8. stage.js and readme.md say 'the one renderer for a CONFIGURED page' and name what is not (the builder, the navigation labs). doc/builder.md has the corrected order - the schema was the blocker and it is fixed, so the remaining four steps start with draw_child - and compare/ is recorded as dropped, with cross/ as the reason. paging.css .paging-stage-flip deleted. Also fixed the stale schema in doc/builder.md's control table and doc/persistence.md's file example.

ITEM 9 NOT DONE, and the reason is a measurement not a shrug. BuildStage -> PagingStage needs three seams, not one: draw_child for a child's panel, and somewhere for Build's crumbs and its sheet title, which sit outside the box. It also means reconciling .build-screen-* against paint()'s own surface classes. That is the L the audit called it, and it would have eaten the proof budget. What I did instead: BuildStage DRAWS the arrangement chrome (a toolbar, a footer, a side panel, an aside) in paging.css's own classes, so step 4's word is visible rather than written-and-ignored - about 30 lines, and the merge deletes them.

ALSO FIXED, one line, because the vocabulary insisted on it and the renderer did not: an arrangement PANEL (rail-left/rail-right) drew the page's CHILDREN, which is exactly what blocks.js says a panel is not. It draws filters on the left and properties on the right now. Visible on /cross/'s bottom row.

FOUND, NOT FIXED, outside the fence: press More, then Code, then a chip in the drawer, and ext/layout's dev DesignTool claims the rail with its own empty state ('Click a box inside any region...'). It only reproduces after two drawer opens in a row. Dev chrome only, and ext/ is another module's file.

CHECKED. 34 pages x 400/1280/1920/3440 = 136 loads, ZERO console errors, no sideways scroll, no literal asterisks - run twice, before and after the last css change. Five doc/readme pages render with zero .md-error. Make's Save round-trips a word to disk and back. A page built in Build (Left rail + Tint + Footer), saved, opened in Make, and changed there changed on disk (navigation rail -> rail-right) and the row read it back; deleted after, and made/ is byte-identical to where it started. assign.outcome:
**Eight of the nine landed. Save saves, both editors speak one language, and every configuration on the wall is now a link you can click.**

![Build, at 3440 — seven controls, step 4 is Arrangement, and the file on the right is the realm's seven words](shots/build-3440.png)

**The throw is gone.** [Make](/imagine/paging/make/)'s **Save** called a function that did not exist, so the whole-tree editor had never once worked. I drove it: changed a word in the JSON box, pressed Save, read the file back off disk, changed it back. It saves.

**Both editors write the same seven words.** [Build](/imagine/paging/build/) had its own five (`style`, `mech`, `kids`, `layout`, `arrange`), so a chip in Build changed nothing at all on a page Make had made. It has no vocabulary of its own now — and its fourth control, which was labelled *Layout* and wrote a key called `arrange` while a different key called `layout` sat unlabelled beside it, is **Arrangement**, the realm's own word. Proven end to end: built a page in Build, saved it, opened it in Make, clicked one chip, and the file on disk changed.

**Nine cells, nine links.** [Cross](/imagine/paging/cross/)'s wall was nine live pages and no way into any of them. Every cell is a link now — and the links did nothing when clicked, for a reason worth writing down: **a page in this realm is built once**, so its stage had already made up its mind before the link existed. It re-reads the address on arrival. The [nest preset](/imagine/paging/library/nest/) finally lights its own chip, links out, and clicks off.

**One bar, eight controls.** The Library's grey *"Pick one of twelve"* button — which read as unset while a page was already running under it — is the bar's eighth dropdown, showing the running page's name. **Code** and **More** were the same button twice; Code opens the drawer on the code.

**Wide screens, in one number.** Four pages opened on **720px of prose inside a 2,739px box** at 3440. They open on content that uses the box: **2,634 of 2,739**.

![Skin at 3440 — the box is full, and both colours are visible](shots/skin-3440.png)

**Left, with the reason.** `BuildStage` should *be* a `PagingStage` and is not yet: it needs three seams rather than the one the plan assumed, and the CSS of two stages has to be reconciled — an afternoon, not an hour, and the schema it was waiting on is now fixed, so the four steps are written down in [doc/builder.md](/imagine/paging/doc/builder/). Meanwhile Build draws the arrangement chrome itself, so the word it writes is a word you can see. One bug found outside my fence: press **More**, then **Code**, then a chip, and the dev DesignTool takes the drawer.

**Checked:** 34 pages x 400 / 1280 / 1920 / 3440 = **136 loads, zero console errors**, no sideways scroll, no stray asterisks — run twice.
